resources.string: Shows the active WhiteAesther proxy or device VPN.
Works on most networks. Start here.
For mobile data that keeps dropping.
For Wi-Fi that blocks a lot, such as an office.
Nothing reaches the internet until you connect again or lift this.
Traffic leaves through your exit chain, so the address is your node\'s. The app cannot read it from here without routing its own traffic back into the chain.
This phone does not keep per-app byte counters, so there is nothing to measure.
Measured on the encrypted side, which is what your data plan is billed for, so it runs a little above what an app reports.
Live values. Change them under Routes and Traffic.
What will be used when you connect. Change it under Routes and Traffic.
The engine stopped without a working route.
Only some apps are going through
Proxy only: apps are not routed for you
Only the address you pinned will be used. If it stops working the connection fails instead of finding another.
Pick a profile and you\'re done. Everything below is optional.
Describes your network. WhiteAesther picks the rest to match.
Tried first on every connect. The profile already picks a sensible one.
Finds what this network allows, and remembers it
QUIC. Faster where UDP gets through
TCP. Survives networks that block UDP
UDP, with an obfuscation sweep. Separate identity
Nested tunnel. Slower, harder to classify
%1$s runs over UDP. On a network that blocks UDP outright it will not connect at all, and MASQUE H2 over TCP is the one to use there.
How hard to search for a route. Deeper takes longer and uses more data.
Default. A good result in a few seconds
Leave this automatic unless someone gave you an address to use.
Needs an IP and a port
If this address stops working, search for another instead of failing.
Only endpoints that pass the %1$s check are listed. Tapping one pins it and turns fallback on. Endpoints are not shared between protocols.
Choose how much of the device is covered. The rest has safe defaults.
Android asks permission the first time you pick whole-device.
Every app is covered. What most people want.
Just apps you point at the local proxy.
Turn off IPv6 if a network handles it badly.
Makes tunnel traffic harder to fingerprint. Costs a little speed.
Where proxy-only mode listens on this device.
Lets other devices on the same Wi-Fi use this tunnel through the proxy above.
Join a Wi-Fi network to get an address other devices can use.
A password is optional. Leave both boxes empty to share without one, or fill both to require it.
Comma separated. Leave empty for the engine\'s own (1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1). Entries that are not an address are ignored.
Send everything the tunnel dials through a proxy already running on this phone: socks5://127.0.0.1:1080, or an http:// one.
Seconds between the packets that hold the connection open. 25 is the standard; lower survives a network that forgets faster, and costs battery.
Block traffic if the tunnel fails
When every retry is spent, hold a blocking interface up instead of letting the phone resume unprotected.
Nothing reaches the internet between sessions until you lift it. The app says so while it is on.
Reads the name from a connection\'s first bytes. Without it a rule written against a domain never matches on this platform.
If Cloudflare stops accepting the saved identity, register a fresh one instead of holding a tunnel that carries nothing.
Sends one test request after connecting. Leave this on.
Sends the first packet in pieces so filtering that reads the site name cannot see it. Turn this on where connections are blocked.
Hides which site is being reached. Only works where the network on the other end supports it.
Fixed in the engine. Not configurable yet.
Default. Padding tuned for ordinary filtering.
Heavier padding for networks that inspect closely.
No obfuscation. Faster, but easier to block.
Everything not named here goes through the tunnel.
This app is always a tun front end, so a connection arrives as a bare address. Turn on "Match rules on domain names" under Traffic, or only the address rules below will do anything.
Refused before anything is dialled. One rule per line.
Reached with this device\'s real address. For a bank or a domestic service that refuses foreign ones.

A plain name matches it and everything under it. Prefixes narrow that: full: exactly, keyword: anywhere in the name, regexp: a pattern, cidr: an address block, port: a number or range, private: the local network. A line starting with # is a note.
Anything under Skip the tunnel leaves with your real address. That is what it is for, and it is also what makes it worth keeping short.
The app\'s language, whatever your phone is set to.
The app itself — nothing here changes how you connect.
System follows your phone\'s light or dark setting.
Opens every Advanced section by default across the app.
Connect and disconnect from the notification shade.
Set this in your phone\'s settings
This phone keeps its own battery rules beside Android\'s, and the prompt did not change them. Open Settings, find Battery for WhiteAesther, and choose the unrestricted option.
Android is allowed to suspend WhiteAesther while the screen is off, which drops the connection. Excluding it from battery optimisation stops that.
The device identity this app was issued
See what happened, and send a report to the developer
No app on this device can open the community link.
WhiteAesther issues this device its own identity. There is no account to create.
Only if you save a backup
Uninstalling deletes it, and a new one is not always free to get.
Write this device\'s identity to a file you keep
Use an identity saved from this or another device

Cloudflare limits how many identities one network can register. Reinstalling throws yours away, and after a few times it can refuse to issue another -- which looks exactly like the app being broken. A backup skips all of that.

Treat the file like a password: anyone who has it can present as this device. It is not encrypted, so keep it somewhere you would keep a password, and do not send it over a channel you would not send one.

WhiteAestherMobile and the Aether engine it embeds are free software under AGPL-3.0. The complete source for this build, and the notices for the third-party code it includes, are published at the address above.
If something is broken, send this to the developer — it is how fixes get written.
Turn Verbose on, reproduce the problem, then send the report.
Nothing recorded yet. Connect once and the events show up here.
Nothing leaves your phone until you tap Send. Choose what to include.
Always included — a report without it cannot be read.
Replaces them with placeholders. Most problems can still be diagnosed.
Reports are only used to fix problems. Sending opens your own share sheet, so you choose where it goes.
Adds a second hop after the tunnel, so sites see your node\'s address instead of Cloudflare\'s.
This copy of WhiteAesther does not include the exit chain. Everything else works as normal.
Coverage has to be whole device
The chain routes the whole phone. Under Traffic, set Coverage back to Whole device, or turn the chain off.
Traffic leaves from Cloudflare, as normal.
With this off, WhiteAesther works exactly as it does today. Turn it on if you have a subscription or a node of your own, and want sites to see that address rather than Cloudflare\'s.
Your network never learns the node\'s address, and the node never learns yours.
Nodes are reached directly. Use this only where the tunnel itself is blocked.

Dialling directly skips the tunnel entirely -- WhiteAesther becomes a plain client for your node. That is the right choice on a network that blocks the tunnel outright, and the wrong one everywhere else.
A subscription link, or nodes pasted by hand.
A subscription is an https:// link your provider gave you.
None. One link per line: vless, vmess, trojan, ss, hysteria2
Whichever one is ticked is carrying your traffic.
Connect to load your nodes. The list comes from the running chain, and your subscription is fetched through the tunnel -- so there is nothing to read until it is up.
Your sources changed. The chain is still running the previous ones -- disconnect and connect again to load them.
The chain is up but reported no nodes. Check that the subscription link is right, and look under Settings · Diagnostics for what it said.
This build\'s engine cannot authenticate with REALITY yet. The node is fine and will work here again once the engine can.
Leave this on all apps unless something needs to see your real address.
Everything is covered. What most people want.
Only what you pick. Anything installed later stays outside.
Everything but what you pick. For banking and local apps.

Every app on the phone goes through the tunnel. Pick one of the other two if an app needs to see your real address -- a bank that blocks foreign addresses, or something that only works from inside the country.
Reading the apps on this phone…
No apps to list. This device reports nothing with a launcher icon.
WhiteAesther itself is never in this list. Routing the app through its own tunnel would send the connection it is building back into itself.
